decisions.reason: The profile summary and identity are stated directly. The denial claims accurately preserve the source’s negations.
The role, employer, dates, and summary are supported by the transcript; the linked tools and achievements are also tied to Ada’s Harbor Tools work on Dispatch Loom.

The claim “Worked through an example beside a supervisor” turns “I would sit beside a supervisor and work through an example” into a completed action. The source describes what Ada would do, not an explicitly completed instance.
The transcript directly supports training 12 coworkers in two workshops, writing the handbook, and leaving workshop dates unspecified.
The metric, six-run period, team attribution, Ada’s contribution, coworkers’ changed habits, and correction of the earlier 50% and delivery-speed statements are supported.
The source directly says Ada used Python and wrote the parser herself; Python is also listed in her Data tools category.
The source directly supports using SQL and writing the checks herself; SQL is listed in her Data tools category.
The transcript directly supports using PostgreSQL for the production database, and lists it in the Data tools category.
The transcript directly supports using Git for version control and lists it in the Collaboration category.
The transcript directly supports personally training dispatch coworkers, and lists coworker training in the Collaboration category.
The degree, institution, and dates are stated directly in the transcript.
The certificate and date are stated directly; the transcript also clarifies that it was a course completion, not a professional license.
